original_snippet: memset(out,0,MAX); v10 = GetArrayLength(v9); GetByteArrayRegion(env, v9, 0, v10, out)
reconstruction_snippet: memset(out,0,max); if (length > max) length = max; GetByteArrayRegion(array, 0, length, out)
explanation: The original copies the whole Java byte array into the buffer with no bound (only the memset is sized by MAX). The port clamps the copy to max. Differs only when the array is longer than MAX, where the original overflows the buffer. Defensive deviation, not a real bug. Also the port adds an env==nullptr early return that the original does not have.

original_snippet: v3 = timestamp + lifetime; return v3 < GetOnline()->counter (+0x28)  [listing: CMP R4,R0; MOVCS 0; MOVCC 1 = unsigned <]
reconstruction_snippet: const std::uint32_t deadline = timestamp_ + lifetime_; return deadline <= COnline::GetInstance()->GetCounter();
explanation: The listing returns expired only when the deadline is strictly below the counter (unsigned LO/CC). The port uses <=, so a message expires one counter tick early, when the deadline equals the counter. ProcessRecvQueue (0x80ad54) relies on this result to mark messages finished.
